strengths: Principled theoretical contribution: Proposition 1 elegantly unifies training-free guidance with Langevin MCMC, providing theoretical justification for the proposed local search strategy
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple domains (planning, offline RL, image generation) demonstrates the breadth and generality of the framework
Practical efficiency gains clearly demonstrated: 2x compute savings in image generation, >90% success rates with global search on planning tasks, competitive performance on D4RL
Well-executed technical framework combining classical search algorithms (BFS/DFS) with diffusion model sampling in an intuitive and effective way
Excellent presentation with clear figures, detailed algorithms, comprehensive appendices, and thorough experimental protocols supporting reproducibility
Addresses an important and timely problem (inference-time control of diffusion models) with practical solutions showing consistent improvements
weaknesses: Limited novelty: individual components (Langevin MCMC, BFS/DFS, training-free guidance) are existing techniques; the contribution is primarily in their combination
Task-specific verifier requirement significantly limits generality; each domain requires custom-designed verifier functions without principled design guidelines
Theoretical contribution (Proposition 1) establishes only continuous-limit equivalence; practical applicability with discrete implementations is unclear
Insufficient analysis of hyperparameter sensitivity; multiple hyperparameters require careful tuning (Table 3) without clear adaptive tuning methodology despite claims
Marginal improvements on several benchmarks, particularly in D4RL (Table 1) where improvements are often modest, raising questions about practical significance
Incomplete analysis of when each search strategy (local/global, BFS/DFS) is beneficial and missing systematic study of compute-quality trade-offs
Limited comparison with recent inference-time scaling methods; primarily compared with simple Best-of-N baseline for image generation
Verifier design details and hacking/adversarial robustness concerns are not adequately addressed; limited discussion of failure modes

strengths: Systematic elucidation of BFS design space (tempering, scoring, resampling) with clear takeaways; prior methods shown to be special cases of unified framework
Novel adaptive DFS algorithm with threshold-based compute allocation demonstrating 2× efficiency gains without prior difficulty knowledge
Rigorous theoretical contribution establishing equivalence between training-free guidance and annealed Langevin MCMC (Proposition 1) with convergence bounds (Theorem 1)
Comprehensive experiments across multiple domains (text-to-image, planning, offline RL) with thorough ablations and reproducibility details in appendices
Clear demonstration of joint scaling benefits over scaling global/local search independently (Figure 4), establishing improved Pareto frontiers
Practical double-verifier strategy for mitigating reward hacking with substantial improvements (FID 155.7→127.8 on ImageNet)
Strong consistent empirical results: improved BFS outperforms prior methods; policy distillation competitive with online RL while significantly faster
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: BFS/DFS for diffusion established in prior SMC/tree search work; improved design combines existing techniques (Increase tempering from DAS, Max scoring from FK-steering, SSP resampling from DAS); Langevin MCMC for compositional generation from Du et al. 2023

Significant gap between theory and practice: Proposition 1 equivalence holds only for T→∞ limit; practical finite-T approximation quality unexplored. Theorem 1 assumes bounded support, strong log-concavity, L-smoothness—unrealistic for complex multimodal distributions; bounds loose with limited actionable guidance

Experimental concerns: BFS ablation improvements often modest/within error bars (Table 1 differences <0.05); unfair baseline comparisons in D4RL where TFG/DAS get 2× compute; when equalized, advantages diminish (Medium HalfCheetah: DAS 53.4 vs TTS 54.8)
Insufficient analysis of when/why joint scaling outperforms proportional allocation—no theoretical characterization or intuitive explanation of compute tradeoffs

Extensive hyperparameter complexity undermines practicality claim: requires tuning τ_t, scoring function, Nrecur, ρ, µ, δ_t, ∆T; Tables 8-9 show substantial sensitivity (performance varies within/near error bars); contradicts 'principled' classical search appeal

DFS design choices lack principled justification: backtracking depth ∆T≥T/4 appears arbitrary; limited ablation on threshold schedule δ_t; concurrent work ABCD claims better sample quality through full denoising but advantages unclear

Limited failure mode analysis: no discussion of when DFS underperforms BFS or guidance for practitioners on method selection; missing comparisons with other search strategies (evolutionary search, MCTS variants)
